answer: Sybil resistance needs an entry cost that scales with identity, not capital. Picture the agent economy as a coastal inlet: every new agent enters through one narrow haven where an existing peer must stake its own reputation as bond. If the newcomer cheats, the sponsor's stake burns, so sponsors audit before vouching. Growth then spreads like a plume of smoke — each new node trails back to a bonded origin — and a sybil farm must find thousands of sponsors willing to risk their own funds, which honest agents simply won't do.
